what_it_does: This chip (IRIS) accelerates mixed-reality headsets that display photorealistic 3D virtual objects in the real world. It handles two heavy computational tasks: learning a 3D model of a room's surfaces from camera video, and rendering those surfaces with realistic light and shadow in real time. The bottleneck is that the 3D model's parameter data (50+ MB) doesn't fit in the chip's fast on-chip memory (4 MB L2 cache), forcing constant slow trips to external memory. IRIS reduces this external memory traffic by compressing the parameter data on-the-fly without losing visual quality, and splits the rendering work into stages that can run in parallel without stalling. It keeps everything fast enough for the tight 15 millisecond deadline required for user comfort.
